description: Base model: behaviour cloning on JPL Horizons 1950-2020 (8 h CPU run). Best on the 2024-2027 test set.
algorithm: Given Moon state s = (x, y, z [km], vx, vy, vz [km/s]) at epoch jd_tdb:
2. obs[10] = (x/r_scale, y/r_scale, z/r_scale, vx/v_scale, vy/v_scale, vz/v_scale, sun/|sun|, |sun|/au_km - 1)
3. a[6] = MLP(obs): for each layer h = W*h + b (W row-major, shape [out, in]); SiLU(h) = h/(1+exp(-h)) after every layer except the last
4. s_next = rk4_two_body(s, step_s, substeps) + a*action_scale.sd + action_scale.mu
5. s_next is the state at jd_tdb + step_s/86400. Repeat for longer horizons (autoregressive; the Sun is always evaluated at the current step's epoch).

constants.rk4_note: classic RK4 on r'' = -mu*r/|r|^3 with h = step_s/substeps

frame: geocentric (Earth centre, 500@399), ecliptic and mean equinox of J2000 (Horizons ECLIPJ2000), geometric states (no light-time / aberration)
time_scale: TDB, Julian date; training grid is 6 h aligned to 00/06/12/18 h TDB

sun_model.reference: J. Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, 2nd ed., ch. 25 (low accuracy solar coordinates), longitude referred to the J2000 equinox by subtracting 1.396971*T deg; latitude = 0.
sun_model.accuracy: max 34.9 arcsec vs JPL Horizons over 2024-2027

precision_note: Trained/evaluated in PyTorch with float32 MLP; test vectors use float64 throughout. Differences between the two are < 1e-5 km per step.
